title: callflow-timeline-investigation
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal timeline and commands I ran while chasing the intermittent function-call parsing failures in streaming responses. This is a scratchpad; not polished. Keep notes of what reproduced reliably and what was a red herring.

High-level symptom (observed intermittently in prod and local staging):
- Some streaming responses that should emit a final JSON function call object come out truncated or with duplicated fragments across chunk boundaries, causing the downstream parser to throw: "Invalid JSON: unexpected token at position X" or "unbalanced braces".
- When caller switches from text->stream to function_call mode, sometimes we see a leading '\n' or extraneous characters (e.g., UTF-8 BOM-like bytes) at the start of the final chunk.

Useful identifiers:
- Reproduce-run-id: replay-20260218-pt1
- Example message-id headers seen in logs: X-Req-Id: 3f7b9c2a

Timeline + commands tried (chronological breadcrumbs):
2026-02-16 09:12 - initial repro in staging (flaky)
- Replayed recorded conversation with streaming enabled. Not reproduced immediately.

2026-02-17 14:03 - forced minimal stream with explicit newline boundaries
- curl command used against local dev proxy to mimic chunking:
  curl -v -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/stream -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-mini", "stream":true, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"call tool with payload"}], "function_call": {"name":"my_tool"}}'
- Observed chunk boundary contents in tcpdump (see sample below).

2026-02-18 10:20 - isolated Python minimal repro (saved as quick_repro_stream.py)
- snippet:
  import requests
  r = requests.post('http://localhost:8080/v1/stream', json={"model":"rwd-mini","stream":True,...}, stream=True)
  for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
      print(repr(chunk))
- Output showed sequences like: b'}{"name":"my_tool","arguments":{"id":123' followed by b',"more":"..."}'
- i.e. closing brace from previous object concatenate with start of next object in the same read.

2026-02-20 16:45 - tried changing chunk_size in requests.iter_content to small (64 bytes)
- reproduction more consistent; parser fails ~ 60% of time; suggests boundary alignment matters.

2026-02-21 11:10 - tried adding a streaming framing layer (newline-delimited JSON) at the server
- server now emits each object as `\n` + JSON + `\n` instead of raw chunked bytes. Parser failures dropped to near-zero in this branch.
- However, this is a protocol change and incompatible with some clients. Not an immediate ship fix.

2026-02-22 09:00 - tested with token-level truncation (simulate early EOF)
- Force: cut stream mid-UTF8 codepoint. Observed decoder on client raises UnicodeDecodeError then the buffered partial JSON gets discarded and we see a different failure mode.

Error snippets captured from logs (sanitized):
- "parser_error: Unexpected token `,` at position 1432 when parsing function_call.arguments"
- "json_decode_error: unbalanced braces, last_char='\\u0000'"
- client-side: "UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 7: invalid start byte"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Underlying stream transport can produce arbitrary byte boundaries; our parser assumes chunk boundary == message boundary in several places.
   - Evidence: changing client chunk_size affects failure rate.
2) Server sometimes emits unexpected control bytes (rare) when buffer flush triggers on specific tokenization ops in runtime (e.g., when swapping kernel path / quantization).
   - Evidence: rare logs show non-printable bytes before JSON object. Need to correlate with kernel-selection logs (GH #4821).
3) UTF-8 / encoding mismatch in the edge path that serializes partial KV-cache dumps while streaming results in stray bytes.
   - Evidence: UnicodeDecodeError in a subset of failures.
4) Client-side incremental decoder logic in SDK throws away partial buffer on error instead of attempting corrective reassembly.
   - Evidence: behavior differs between requests.iter_content chunk sizes and node-fetch stream implementations.

Repro cases and minimal examples to run locally (commands):
- Python requests stream test (quick_repro_stream.py). Steps:
  1) Start local runtime with debug dumps enabled (export RWD_STREAM_DEBUG=1)
  2) Run: python quick_repro_stream.py > stream_dump.txt
  3) Inspect stream_dump.txt for chunk boundary patterns and control bytes (hexdump -C stream_dump.txt)

- Curl with raw TCP capture:
  1) sudo tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -w dump.pcap port 8080 &
  2) run the curl POST (see above)
  3) stop tcpdump and open in Wireshark; filter by tcp.analysis.flags and follow TCP stream. Look for patterns where JSON begins mid-packet.

Quick debugging notes (observations + quick fixes tried):
- Adding newline framing at server eliminates ambiguity; simple and robust for our current parsers.
- Implemented a tolerant-JSON-assembler in the alpha SDK: buffer bytes and try to regex-extract `{.*}` blocks across reads; helped but produced false positives on nested JSON in text fields.
- Swapping out the incremental JSON decoder for the Node SDK to an alternative library improved resilience to chunk-splitting around multibyte UTF-8 chars.

Potential root cause path (most likely):
- A combination of streaming transport chunking + an opportunistic small binary blob occasionally injected by internal debug code (KV dump), causing a non-UTF8 byte to appear between chunks. The SDK then decodes the stream assuming UTF-8 and fails fast, discarding buffer. On next chunk the parser sees a partial JSON and errors.

Short-term mitigations (practical, low-risk):
- Server: opt-in newline-delimited JSON mode for streaming endpoints (feature flag) and document behavior. Immediately usable by SDKs.
- SDK: implement a more conservative incremental decoder: keep previous buffer on decode errors, attempt to resync at next `{` or `\n{` instead of dropping. Add 3 retries for resync with exponential backoff on streaming parse failures.
- Runtime: guard any internal binary debug dumps with a separate control channel (do not interleave with main stdout).

Long-term fixes (requires coordinated change):
- Agree on a streaming wire protocol (ndjson or explicit length-prefixed frames). Update hosted API and SDKs together.
- Add end-to-end test harness: fuzz chunk boundaries with multibyte sequences and control bytes to ensure parser robustness across SDKs.
- Add telemetry metric: stream_parse_recoveries and stream_parse_fatal, attach to request-id for tracing.

Test matrix to add to CI (quick list):
- ndjson mode on/off across SDKs (python/node/go)
- chunk boundary fuzz (sizes: 1, 2, 16, 64, 1024) for multi-byte UTF-8 sequences
- injected non-printable bytes at random positions in stream (0x00, 0x80, 0xFF)
- early EOF mid-codepoint and mid-object

Notes for next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Get kernel-selection logs correlated with failure replay id replay-20260218-pt1 (ask @Maya to pull infra logs)
- [ ] Implement feature-flagged ndjson output on runtime (branch: feat/stream-ndjson)
- [ ] Add resyncing incremental decoder to node and python SDKs (Ethan to own node PR)
- [ ] Write small e2e fuzz harness and add to CI (low priority until ndjson opt-in done)

Random findings / stray ideas (not yet validated):
- Could use a lightweight CRC field per frame so client can quickly detect frame corruption and request retransmit or switch to non-streaming fallback.
- Consider adding a `stream-continuation` header with sequence numbers to help reassembly in proxies.

Appendix: sample raw chunks (hex-escaped for readability) captured 2026-02-17:
- chunkA: "7b226e616d65223a226d795f746f6f6c222c2261726773223a7b226964223a3132337d7d"  (which decodes to {"name":"my_tool","args":{"id":123}})
- chunkB: "7d7b226e616d65223a" ("}{\"name\":") -> observed when two objects were tightly emitted and network read merged them
- chunkC: "80ff..." (non-utf bytes seen once)

If anyone else is troubleshooting, please drop notes here (append with your timestamp). I'll push the ndjson feature flag branch this week and file SDK issues for the resync decoder.

-- Priya
